feedback.problem:
The displacement $s,$ in meters, relative to a fixed origin $O$ of a particle moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis is given by $s(t)=\sqrt{t}\,(\operatorname{ln}⁡t-2),$ where $t>0$ is the time measured in seconds. Determine the time intervals in which the particle is moving in the direction of increasing $x.$

$t\in (${{field-1}},

{{field-2}}$)$
feedback.worked_solution:
If the particle moves in the direction of increasing $x,$ then its velocity is positive. 

First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}\,(\sqrt{t}\,(\operatorname{ln}⁡t-2)) \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡t-2}{2\sqrt{t}}+\sqrt{t}\cdot \frac{1}{t} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡t-2}{2\sqrt{t}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{t}} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡t}{2\sqrt{t}}-\frac{2}{2\sqrt{t}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{t}} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡t}{2\sqrt{t}}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{t}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{t}} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡t}{2\sqrt{t}}\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate time intervals in which the particle is moving in the direction of increasing $x$, we solve the inequality $v(t)>0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & >0 \\ \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡t}{2\sqrt{t}} & >0 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡t & >0 \\ t & >{e}^{0} \\ t & >1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the time interval in which the particle is moving in the direction of increasing $x$ is 

$$
t\in (1,\infty ).
$$
